deals.body:
Only price reductions are promos (percent off, multi-buy, coupon, price below regular_unit_price). Shipping fees, minimum orders, pack options and other remarks go in source_note, never in promo. A promo is a price with an end date. Record it, watch it, and drop it when it ends.
- Store on every promo price: promo (label), promo_until (YYYY-MM-DD, or leave empty if unknown), regular_unit_price (the normal shelf price per unit), requires_program (loyalty program id, if the price needs a card or app).
- If promo_until is in the past, the app ranks the item at regular_unit_price. If there is no regular price, the row leaves the ranking and shows Promo ended until re-checked.
- If promo_until is missing, treat the promo as short-lived and re-check within 14 days.
- Flag promos ending within 3 days so an active daily-driver deal can be used or stocked up on.
- Do not stock up on perishables because of a discount. Stock up only when a daily driver is non-perishable and the saving is real (about 20% or more below the regular price).
- Rossmann style 10 percent coupons, REWE Bonus-Booster and Netto app coupons rotate. Record them as promos with an end date, never as the normal price.
- App-only or card-only prices are valid only if the program is free and easy. Mark them with requires_program.
- Observed 2026-10-24: PX Mart raw chicken at NT$846 for 1.8 kg (regular NT$711/kg) has no end date, so re-check within 14 days. Costco Korea prices need the membership (costco-kr-membership); its fee is still unverified.
- Mixed packs (Costco kimchi 2.9 kg = 2 kg cabbage + 0.9 kg radish kimchi) are priced per total kg and flagged as mixed.
- Package weight can vary (PX Mart ±10%): record the stated weight and note the tolerance.
deals.title: Deals and promo expiry

health.body:
NUTRITION DATA (2026-10-24): per 100 g, USDA FoodData Central SR Legacy via getfoodfacts.com, stored on products[].nutrition with scope generic_reference, form, source_url and retrieved_at. Stored: eggs, Greek yoghurt (nonfat), salmon (wild raw), cod, sardines (canned in oil), tuna (light, in oil), beef 95% lean, broccoli, kale, blueberries, strawberries, brown rice, oats (partial, fibre undeclared), quinoa, walnuts, flaxseed, turmeric, cayenne, pumpkin seeds (macros only); earlier: chicken breast, lentils, spinach, Ottogi ramen. Still missing: celery, black pepper, chilli, lemon juice, chia, pangasius, rice, tortillas, salsa, kimchi, harzer, linseed oil, grilled chicken. Generic values differ from branded packs; the Patagonia salmon is farmed and the stored salmon values are wild.
Each item has a health tag: core, ok or limit.
- core: supports lean and the userar goals (lean protein, fish, eggs, plain dairy, legumes, veg, berries, oats, nuts and seeds). Buy these first and compare hardest.
- ok: neutral, fine in normal amounts (spices, household, grooming, most skincare).
- limit: buy rarely or choose carefully (added sugar, heavy processing, high salt, refined flour).
Rules when choosing a product inside an item:
- Prefer plain, short ingredient lists. For yoghurt choose plain Greek, no added sugar. For salsa and chilli choose low sugar. For tortillas choose wholegrain where available.
- Fish: prefer wild salmon, sardines and cod. Tuna is fine in moderation (mercury). Pangasius is parked.
- Oils: cold-pressed linseed oil must stay chilled and fresh. Check best-before.
- Never recommend a cheaper product that adds sugar, trans fats or heavy processing just to win the ranking. Show it, but not as BEST for health.
- Nutrition is stored per product (products[].nutrition) with scope: label (product label), generic_reference (USDA-style table), press_release or estimate. Label beats reference. Never fill a value from memory.
- Compare protein per euro using nutrition.values.protein_g and energy_kcal where present. Verified so far: chicken breast raw, lentils raw, spinach raw (USDA), Ottogi High Protein Cup Noodles (press release: Rose 170 kcal / 12 g protein, Mala 150 kcal / 12 g protein per cup).
- Core additions: chicken breast (daily, core), healthy rice (brown or mixed grain, daily, core). Kimchi, white rice and healthy ramen are ok: watch salt in kimchi and instant noodles.
- Healthy ramen means low kcal and high protein per cup, judged on the label, not the marketing.
health.title: Health rubric

loyalty.body:
COSTCO KOREA: the user has no membership, so costco-kr is flagged needs_membership and excluded by default in the Stores filter; its prices stay in the database but do not appear in comparisons unless he ticks it. Membership fee still unverified.
Use only free programs that match what is actually bought. Paid programs (Coupang WOW) must save more than they cost.
- Germany: REWE Bonus (free, app), Rossmann app (free coupons), Netto plus app (free, PAYBACK), dm with PAYBACK, Amazon Spar-Abo for repeat orders.
- Slovakia: Lidl Plus (free, app), Kaufland Card XTRA (free), Tesco Clubcard (free), dm.
- Korea: Coupang WOW (paid monthly), E-mart and Shinsegae Point, Olive Young with CJ ONE, Naver Plus.
- Taiwan: PX Mart welfare points (free via app), Carrefour member card, Watsons membership.
- Each program has a status: verified (read on the official page on the date shown), partial (some facts read), or unverified (page not readable, facts must be checked before relying on them). See the Guide list for details.
- When a price needs a program, a card or app must be in hand before the price counts as available to the user.
- Only Costco Korea membership and its price effect were seen in use on 2026-10-24. Costco fee, CJ ONE, E-mart and Coupang WOW details remain unverified because those sites block automated reading.
- Programs are only updated when the official page was read in that run (verified_at).
loyalty.title: Loyalty programs and cards

principles.body:
Value = price per kg / l / piece in EUR, after checking a promo has not expired. Pack price is never the comparison.
Comparison unit follows how the item is bought: weight (per kg), liquids (per l), counted things (per piece).
Health first: a cheaper product with added sugar or heavy processing is shown, but never ranked best for health.
Daily drivers are tracked tightly; one-off purchases only when cheap to check.
Stale data is not a price: older than 90 days, or an ended promo, counts as unknown until re-checked.
Only price reductions are promos. Shipping, minimum orders and pack options go in the note.
Prices are append-only: a changed price is a new row; an unchanged price only gets a new checked date.
Every price has an origin (yours or auto) and a source.
principles.title: Buying principles

sources.body:
KOREA BASELINE (2026-10-24): Korea Consumer Agency 참가격 생필품 가격 정보, data.go.kr dataset 15083256 (https://www.data.go.kr/data/15083256/fileData.do). Free, no usage limits; CSV downloadable without login (encoding cp949; columns 상품명, 조사일, 판매가격, 판매업소, 제조사, 세일여부, 원플러스원); 592 packaged products, 448 stores, two survey dates per file (2026-09-11 and 2026-09-25), updated monthly, next 2026-11-13. Open API needs a data.go.kr account, 활용신청 and a service key. Chains in the file: GS더프레시, 롯데슈퍼, 이마트xx점 (hypermarket), 이마트24(본사) (convenience, NOT E-Mart), GS25(본사), CU(본사), 세븐일레븐(본사), 농협, 현대백화점, 신세계백화점; no Homeplus, no fresh produce, no chicken breast, yoghurt, oats or nuts. Imported as one median price per chain per date (ids kca-*), origin auto, source_type dataset, with product_name. Prices are survey prices, not live shelf prices. Re-import each month from a fresh CSV supplied by the user. Naver shopping API: Naver API Hub covers search and shopping insight (click trends); whether the older shopping search API with prices is still free is unverified.
FETCH RULE (2026-10-24): WebFetch only opens URLs that came from WebSearch or that the user pasted; stored product URLs (Rossmann, Netto, Amazon short links, hddfs, Bodfeld) cannot be re-read automatically. For nutrition use getfoodfacts.com (USDA SR Legacy, works); nutritionvalue.org errors; recipal values are derived per-cup, do not use.
THE REGISTER: every source is a document in the collection source_register (name, country, type, url, access, status, five 1-5 scores, 0-100 score, confidence tested/reported/untested, scope, update frequency, EAN/unit price/promo dates, key or membership needed, note, evidence_url, last_tested). It is shown in the Guide tab and ranked by score. After testing any source, update its status, scores, confidence, last_tested, note and updated_at, and recompute score = round(20 x (0.30 coverage + 0.25 reliability + 0.20 ease + 0.15 freshness + 0.10 cost)). Add newly found sources as new documents.
BIGGEST OPPORTUNITIES (2026-10-24): 1) Slovakia: cenyslovensko.sk, the state food price comparator (reported down after a cyberattack in Dec 2025, check if back). 2) Korea: official price.go.kr and its data.go.kr OpenAPI (free service key), plus Naver Shopping API (needs the user's free key). 3) Germany: dm.de and idealo.de are the next fetch tests; REWE needs a market ID. 4) Taiwan: no government price portal found; test PChome, momo, Carrefour and Costco TW via search hits.
KEYS NEEDED FROM the user: data.go.kr service key, Naver developers client ID and secret, a REWE market ID.

Fetch playbook: where prices and nutrition can be read, and what failed. Status is as tested on 2026-10-24 from the cloud research session (WebSearch plus WebFetch only, no logged-in browser). Update this doc whenever a run learns something new.

HOW TO FETCH
- WebFetch only opens URLs that came from a WebSearch result or were given by the user. Search first with the retailer name plus the product (Korean, Traditional Chinese, Slovak or German terms), then fetch the hit.
- Pages are fetched one or two at a time. Bursts trigger client_error or rate limits. Never retry a failed page in the same run.
- Accept a price only if the page shows pack size and price. Record the page URL in source_url. A search snippet alone is not a price.
- If a site is blocked, write research_attempt on the placeholder row and move on. Ask the user for a shelf photo instead of retrying.

KOREA
- Costco Korea (costco.co.kr): WORKS. Product pages show price and weight. Needs membership (costco-kr-membership). Verified chicken, kimchi, rice.
- Coupang (coupang.com): BLOCKED (robots). Only search snippets. Ask for photo or app screenshot.
- E-mart / SSG, CJ ONE, Olive Young: BLOCKED or client_error. Unresolved.
- Naver Shopping: untested. Try via search hits for price comparison.

TAIWAN
- PX Mart online (pxbox.es.pxmart.com.tw): WORKS via search hits. Verified raw chicken (promo, no end date, so re-check within 14 days).
- Carrefour TW, Watsons TW, PChome: untested.

GERMANY
- REWE: product pages show NO price (price depends on the store). Treat as not found unless the user gives a market ID or photo.
- Rossmann: BLOCKED (robots). Needs photo or app coupon screenshot.
- Netto: no product price found by search.
- Picnic: login wall. Amazon, Temu: BLOCKED. Kleinanzeigen: used market only, not a staple price.
- dm, Lidl DE, Kaufland DE, Aldi: untested. Try dm.de and lidl.de product pages first.

SLOVAKIA
- Lidl SK, Tesco, Kaufland, dm SK: untested. Weekly flyer pages (letak) are a likely source for promos with end dates.

NUTRITION
- nutritionvalue.org (USDA data): partly works. 3 of 17 pages read, the rest returned client_error. Retry later, one page per run step.
- Open Food Facts API: not on the fetch allowlist. Open Food Facts product pages only if surfaced by search.
- Brand pages: Ottogi press release gave kcal and protein per cup only (scope press_release). Label values beat reference tables.
- Other reference databases to try: Danish Frida, Swiss naehrwertdaten.ch, Korean RDA food composition DB.
- Never fill a value from memory.

CANDIDATE AGGREGATORS (ideas from another assistant's answer on 2026-10-24, NOT yet tested here; try via search hits and record the result)
- Korea: Naver Shopping (official search API lists products, prices and merchants but needs an API key from the user), Danawa (danawa.com) price comparison.
- Taiwan: PChome 24h, momo, ECPRO price-history comparison (coverage and accuracy unknown).
- Slovakia: Heureka.sk comparison pages and retailer flyers.
- Germany: idealo.de comparison pages, retailer flyers.
- Rule: an aggregator price counts only if it names the retailer, the pack size and the date. Match exact product and size before use.
- Scope: monitor the 15 to 20 daily-driver products tightly first; widen only when data quality is good.

SHELF SCAN (photo import, built 2026-10-24): the + Price button opens Scan shelf. Many photos can be shot in a row and each photo may hold many tags. Claude reads every legible tag, detects the store (signage, logos, receipt), matches tags to known items and products, and the page runs quality checks before anything is saved. Checks: tag unit price versus price divided by size (6 percent tolerance), unit not matching the item's base unit, missing size or unit price, low reader confidence (below 0.7), currency not matching the store's country, missing exchange rate, price more than 3 times above or below the usual price for that item in the country, duplicate in the same scan, promo without end date (info only), tag with no matching item (new item, off by default), store not chosen. Clean rows are pre-selected; flagged rows are off and show red or amber chips. Unchanged prices (within 1 percent) only refresh the checked date; changed prices become a new row and show the percent versus the last price. Each row also shows Cheapest, First price, or percent versus the best other shop in that country. Accepted photo prices are origin user, source type photo, with the photo stored; rows accepted despite a warning keep the warning in the flag field. New stores are created as offline; correct the name and kind afterwards. Multi-buy promos (1+1) are stored with the single-pack shelf price and the offer text as promo.

PASTE AND DROP: Scan shelf accepts images pasted anywhere on the page (Ctrl/Cmd+V, or long-press the paste box on a phone and tap Paste), dropped files, camera shots and chosen files, several at a time. Pasting with nothing open starts a scan. Screenshots of other apps, flyers and online shop pages work the same way and are stored as source type photo, so label them in the note when the source is an online shop. Tall screenshots are scaled so the text stays readable (short side at least 1200 px, long side at most 4000 px).

BEST WORKAROUND: the user photographs shelf prices or labels in the app (source_type photo). That is faster than any blocked site.
sources.title: Where to fetch prices (sources playbook)
